chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), that he said:
If wives of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) had not been forbidden to the people, because of the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty:
And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah or to marry his wives after him, ever.
Marriage was forbidden for al-Hasan and al-Husayn (peace be upon them), because of His saying, Exalted and Mighty:
And do not marry what your fathers married from the women.
So it is not suitable for a man to marry his grandfather's wife.

key_terms.لِقَوْلِ اللَّهِ: Because of the saying of Allah

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to marry his grandfather's wife in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the juristic principle of *qiyas* (analogical reasoning) by comparing the permanent prohibition of the Prophet's wives upon the general public to the prohibition of a grandfather's wife for his grandson. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on deriving specific familial restrictions from the broader Quranic injunctions regarding *mahram* relationships, specifically linking the verse on the Prophet's wives (33:53) with the verse on fathers' wives (4:23) to establish a consistent legal precedent.
